newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Tight supply to keep prices high.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Tight supply to keep prices high.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to firm up this week due to tight supplies in the Philippines, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"It's starting to brighten up in the Mindanao area but I only I expect copra arrivals in the oil mills in two weeks at the latest," said a trader in a U.S.-based commodity house.
Intermittent rains on the southern island of Mindanao in the past several days had slowed down copra deliveries to the mills, traders said.
Mindanao accounts for 55 percent of Philippine coconut output and 80 percent of the country's coconut oil exports, said one trader.
Coconut oil prices are in fact higher in Manila than prices quoted in Europe, said another trader.
The Manila vegetable oil dealer said coconut oil is currently traded at $795 per tonne in Manila as against the $725 per tonne FOB price of the commodity for nearby months in Europe.
Philippine coconut oil exports in March could fall below 50,000 tonnes, said one trader.

Trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines (UCAP) said coconut oil exports from February 1 to 19 reached 50,200 tonnes. Exports in the whole month of February in 1996 reached 63,625 tonnes.

Earlier, UCAP said Philippine coconut oil exports in January this year reached 85,000 tonnes from the year-ago 74,074 tonnes. But Manila traders said coconut export numbers in January 1997 included a carry-over of 29,000 tonnes from December 1996.
Manila vegetable oil traders said tight supplies of coconut oil in the Philippines have been offset by increased deliveries from Indonesia.
"Indonesia shipped out 30,000 tonnes of coconut oil in January and more than 50,000 tonnes this month," a trader said.
"For March, it is uncertain if Indonesia's rising exports can compensate reduced exports from the Philippines," a trader said.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam dropped to 24,625 tonnes as of February 18 from the 28,886 tonne level as of February 10.

Last week, UCAP said coconut oil dropped to an average of $763.50 per tonne CIF from the previous week's $776.50 per tonne despite wide expectations in the Philippines that it would rise. Traders attributed the drop to high stocks in Rotterdam.
